text:
The act of State doctrine provides that courts of one country generally will not examine the validity of a foreign sovereign's official acts taken within its own territory, based on comity and respect for sovereign equality (e.g., *Banco Nacional de Cuba v. Sabbatino*). It does not mean all State acts attract immunity, nor that courts are well placed to assess alleged State torts. Neither of the two offered options correctly states the doctrine.

CONFIDENCE: 85
